newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Takarekbank sell-off expected by Q1 1997.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Takarekbank sell-off expected by Q1 1997.

text.p: Hungary wishes to complete the sell-off of savings cooperative bank Takarekbank by the first quarter of 1997, the bank's general director said on Monday.

"(State privatisation agency APV) would like to complete the privatisation of the bank by the end of the first quarter of next year at the latest" Zsolt Hernadi told a news conference, held after the bank's extraordinary shareholders' meeting.

He added that while the privatisation strategy had not yet been finalised, the state would not retain any stake in the bank and Takarekbank's role as the main bank of savings cooperatives would be maintained.

He said it had also became clear that the bank's current 1.34 billion forint share capital had to be raised, either as part of the privatisation transaction or by asking for guarantees from the buyer for a later equity increase.
APV was expected to announce the tender conditions by the end of October, he added.
Hernadi said a capital increase of around two billion forints would be desirable, not from an operational point of view but because the bank's capital was low.
The capital adequacy ratio of the bank, which operates profitably, stood at 18.4 percent at the end of June, he said.
Hernadi said APV had allowed three potential strategic investors access to a summary of the bank's financial data.
These were Germany's DG Bank, which on Sunday said it was in talks about the purchase of Takarekbank, Austria's GiroCredit and insurance company Hungaria Biztosito Rt, the Hungarian unit of Allianz.
Hernadi said the bank's board had raised the annual unconsolidated pre-tax profit target to 400 million forints from the original plan of 314 million forints.
According to unaudited figures, the bank had a 1996 first half net profit of 266 million forints.
The agenda of the extraordinary general meeting also included personnel issues, while the meeting dropped a point on amendment of the bank's statute.
The bank is 65.98 percent owned by the finance ministry, for which APV acts as owner, while savings cooperatives hold around 32 percent.
